title: My Favorite Husband
paragraphs: Lucille Ball and Richard Denning star as Liz and George Cooper in a domestic situation comedy about marriage, neighbors, misunderstandings, and everyday life.
Domestic situation comedy starring Lucille Ball and Richard Denning. The early Cugat identity evolved into Liz and George Cooper; later ensemble includes Rudolph and Iris Atterbury.
The run breaks into several distinct periods: CBS weekly radio run (July 23, 1948 to March 31, 1951) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Lucille Ball (performer), Richard Denning (performer), Isabel Scott Rorick (creator and writer), [[person|gale-gordon|Gale Gordon]] (performer), Hans Conried (performer), Ruth Perrott (performer), and Frank Nelson (performer).

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]], and [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]].

The stories often return to jealousy and romantic misunderstanding, domestic household life, marriage and couple relationships, social status and clubs, household money and spending, and workplace and boss relationships.
The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Cugat-to-Cooper middle-class refocus, Atterbury ensemble expansion, and Production bridge to I Love Lucy.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|screen-directors-playhouse|Screen Directors Playhouse]], [[show|the-railroad-hour|The Railroad Hour]], [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]], and [[show|the-whistler|The Whistler]].
